disposition_reason: Lead, cadmium and mercury in 984 bivalve samples (mussels, carpet-shell clams, cupped oysters) from Sardinian official controls, by species and production area.

study.design: official monitoring and control of live bivalve molluscs (pre-marketing classification/monitoring of production areas and marketing controls)
study.origin: Sardinian shellfish production areas (Olbia, Ogliastra, Cagliari, Sulcis-Iglesiente, Oristano)
study.market: 385 samples taken at marketing stage by local health authority veterinary services, Sardinia
study.method: microwave acid digestion (EPA 3052); ICP-MS (Agilent 7500CE) per EPA 6020A, isotopes 208Pb, 111Cd, 202Hg, internal standards 209Bi and 115In
study.qa: reagent blanks and CRM 278 and DOLT-2 in each sequence; method accredited ISO/IEC 17025; recoveries not printed

controls.outcome: Pb semester difference significant for mussels (P<0.0001) and clams (P=0.0049); Cd only for clams (P=0.0055); Hg only for mussels (P<0.0001); higher in winter/spring; monthly values figure-only (Figura 2)

controls.comparator: mussels vs carpet-shell clams vs oysters

unresolved: Interquartile ranges are printed only as widths; recorded in notes of the median findings.
Trend regression lines (e.g. Pb y=-0.0006x+0.2407) are not concentrations; not recorded.
Detection limits not printed; text says Cd values lay between the detection limit and one quarter of the maximum level.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum levels (Reg. 1881/2006) for bivalves: Pb 1.5, Cd 1.0, Hg 0.50 mg/kg fresh weight
regulatory_or_exposure.value: exceeded in one sample (Pb, taken during production-area classification); three other samples above two thirds of the Pb limit; Cd all below one quarter of the limit; Hg all below 5% of the limit
